####################################################################################################
Purpose:
- Extract metadata from ClinicalTrials.gov into a SQLite database (only available for 189 out 
of 265 studies).
- (Experimental) Summarize information using OpenAI GPT.

Output:
- `stu_meta_ctgov.rds`: Data frame containing metadata of GSK studies with protocol information.
- `stu_meta_ctgov_query_n.rds`: Data frame containing query length for each NCT link.
- `stu_meta_ctgov_query_success.rds`: Data frame containing query success status for each NCT link.
- `stu_meta_ctgov_sqlite.rds`: SQLite database with successful queries for each NCT link.
- `stu_meta_ctgov_criteriaeligibility.csv`: Data frame containing eligibility criteria per study.
- `stu_meta_ctgov_criteriaincluexclu.csv`: Data frame with two columns, separating eligibility 
criteria into inclusion and exclusion criteria per study.
####################################################################################################

# Set wd to project directory
```{r setup}
rm(list = ls())
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = '~/Nextcloud/Projects/_seas_imm/code_exp_imm')
```

# Load packages, themes, directories, and functions
```{r}
source("00_pck.R")
library("ctrdata")
library("RSQLite")
library("jsonlite")
library("httr")
```

# Load metadata sourced from GSK to obtain the links to databases
```{r}
stu_meta_gsk <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_meta_gsk.rds"))
```

# Extract metadata from ClinicalTrials.gov using the "ctrdata" package
This section uses the NCT id, or if not available the GSK id, from the clinical trials to access the 
database of clinicaltrials.gov.
Only when the query is accessing the unique corresponding study, we accessed the data (189 out of 265 
studies).
We create a SQLite database with a collection holding the data of all accessed studies. This data 
includes information of the participants, rct, results, etc. 
We only used this data to check for the inclusion and exclusion criteria, but this was later doubled 
checked in the protocols. 
```{r}
# Tidy up the NCT ID
stu_nctid <- stu_meta_gsk %>%
  select(study, nctid) %>%
  mutate(nctid = str_replace(nctid, " .*", ""))

# Filter to only include studies with non-missing NCT IDs (189 studies)
filter(stu_nctid, !is.na(nctid)) # 189 studies

# Check the URLs for each study using NCT ID or study ID
ctgov_query_n <- pomp::bake(glue("{dirs$processed}/00_meta_ctgov/stu_meta_ctgov_query_n.rds"), {
  stu_query_n <- list()
  for(i in 1:length(stu_nctid$study)) {
    q_study <- ctrGetQueryUrl(url = glue("id={stu_nctid$study[i]}"), register = "CTGOV2")
    q_nctid <- ctrGetQueryUrl(url = glue("id={stu_nctid$nctid[i]}"), register = "CTGOV2")
    stu_query_n[[i]] <- list(
      "study" = stu_nctid$study[i],
      "q_study" = ctrLoadQueryIntoDb(queryterm = q_study, only.count = TRUE)$n,
      "q_nctid" = ctrLoadQueryIntoDb(queryterm = q_nctid, only.count = TRUE)$n)
  }
  return(stu_query_n)
})

# Check if more than one ID can be used for querying (we only access records when only 1 URL is 
# available)
bind_rows(ctgov_query_n) %>%
  left_join(stu_nctid, by = join_by(study)) %>%
  filter(q_nctid != 1) %>%
  filter(q_study != 1)

# Connect to the SQLite database and choose a collection (table)
db_ctgov <- nodbi::src_sqlite(dbname = glue("{dirs$processed}/00_meta_ctgov/stu_meta_ctgov_sqlite.sql"), 
                              collection = "ctgov") 

# Create the database if it does not exist yet
if (length(dbListTables(db_ctgov$con)) == 0) {

db_query_l <- list()
  for(i in 1:length(stu_nctid$study)) {
    # Obtain URL for the study from NCT ID
    q_study <- ctrGetQueryUrl(url = glue("id={stu_nctid$nctid[i]}"), register = "CTGOV2")
    # If NCT ID is not available (more than 1 ID found in querying), try using study ID
    if(ctrLoadQueryIntoDb(queryterm = q_study, only.count = TRUE)$n != 1) {
      q_study <- ctrGetQueryUrl(url = glue("id={stu_nctid$study[i]}"), register = "CTGOV2")
    }
    # Only if one URL is available, retrieve records and download into database
    if(ctrLoadQueryIntoDb(queryterm = q_study, only.count = TRUE)$n == 1) {
      db_query <- ctrLoadQueryIntoDb(queryterm = q_study, con = db_ctgov)
      db_query_l[[i]] <- list("study" = stu_nctid$study[i],
                              "n" = db_query$n,
                              "success" = db_query$success,
                              "failed" = db_query$failed,
                              "queryterm" = db_query$queryterm)
    } }
}

# Load and save query success information
db_query_success <- pomp::bake(glue("{dirs$processed}/00_meta_ctgov/stu_meta_ctgov_query_success.rds"), {
  bind_rows(db_query_l)
})

# Obtain metadata of the GSK studies (sourced from clinicaltrialsgov) and save as an RDS file
stu_meta_ctgov <- pomp::bake(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_meta_ctgov.rds"), {
  dbGetFieldsIntoDf("protocolSection", con = db_ctgov) %>%
  rename(success = "_id") %>%
  left_join(db_query_success) %>%
  select(study, success, everything()) 
})

# Close the database connection
dbDisconnect(db_ctgov$con)
# Optionally, delete the SQLite database file
# unlink(db_ctgov$dbname)
```

# Extract information using OpenAI GPT (experimental)
```{r}
# Function to ask GPT to summarize metadata from ClinicalTrials.gov
fun_askgpt <- function(fun_data_df = stu_meta_ctgov, fun_prompt = "ask", api_key = api_key) {
  # Arguments:
  # - fun_data_df: (data frame) Text on which to base the response
  # - fun_prompt: (string) Question/Prompt to send to GPT
  # - api_key: (string) API key for OpenAI GPT
  # Output:
  # - result: (string) GPT answer
  
  # Send a request to the OpenAI GPT API
  response <- POST(
    url = "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions", # API endpoint
    add_headers(Authorization = paste("Bearer", api_key)), # API key for authorization
    encode = "json", # Request body encoding
    # Request 
    body = list(
      model = "gpt-4o-mini", # Model to use (see https://platform.openai.com/docs/models)
      temperature = 0, # Control the creativity of the response
      messages = list(
        list(role = "user", content = fun_prompt),  # User's prompt
        list(role = "assistant", content = paste0("vectorstore:", toJSON(fun_data_df))) # Data on which to base the response
        )
      ))
  
  # Parse the response
  result <- content(response, as = "parsed")
  # Return the answer as a string
  return(result$choices[[1]]$message$content)
}

# API key for OpenAI GPT
api_key <- "sk-proj-9wN8Jd69zHiPkQe1K8E8T3BlbkFJJN3KljiZY76fLQ6t1E9a"

# Extract only inclusion and exclusion criteria
ctgov_inclusionexclusion <- stu_meta_ctgov %>%
  select(study, success, protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria) %>%
  rename(inclusion = protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria) %>%
  mutate(
    inclusion = str_remove_all(tolower(inclusion), "\n|\\*"),
    exclusion = str_remove_all(inclusion,".*exclusion|criteria: "),
    inclusion = str_remove_all(inclusion,"exclusion.*|inclusion criteria: "))

# Write CSV file with eligibility criteria
write.csv(select(stu_meta_ctgov, study, success, protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria), 
          glue("{dirs$processed}/00_meta_ctgov/stu_meta_ctgov_criteriaeligibility.csv"))
# Write CSV file with inclusion and exclusion criteria
write.csv(ctgov_inclusionexclusion, 
          glue("{dirs$processed}/00_meta_ctgov/stu_meta_ctgov_criteriaincluexclu.csv"))

# Use GPT to analyze the inclusion and exclusion criteria
answers <- list()
for (i in 1:2) {
  answers[[i]] <- lapply(c(
    "Does the inclusion criteria mentiones previous vaccination or doses or biologicals? Answer with a quote",
    "Does the inclusion criteria requires previous vaccination or doses or biologicals? Answer with a quote"), 
    function(x) {  
      c(fun_askgpt(fun_data_df = ctgov_inclusionexclusion[i, "inclusion"], 
                        fun_prompt = x, api_key))
    })
}

# Flatten the list of answers into a single vector
unlist(answers, recursive = TRUE)
```
